page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 8825.18 and a PassMark CPU score of 10041.11. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1109.08 and poor single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 19.15 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth remains stable, measuring 60.77 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 49.44 GB/sec for large-block writes. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 11.0 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 6.35 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.e3.xlarge offers a high density of RAM relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require cutting-edge single-thread CPU performance. Given the weak single-core metrics and database operation benchmarks, this instance is best suited for caching layers, memory-intensive backend services, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded general-purpose applications.
